valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E (FY2027E adjusted diluted EPS viewed at the 12-month target date)

bear.driver: Persistent Engines & Power Systems supply-chain bottlenecks force OE prioritization over higher-margin aftermarket, while standalone corporate costs weigh on margins.

base.driver: Gradual supplier recovery and 5%-7% organic growth on the $19.3B backlog drive modest operating leverage off the FY2026E pro forma adjusted EPS midpoint of $7.93.

bull.driver: Faster multisourcing integration unlocks commercial aftermarket mix and stronger free cash flow conversion.

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY2027E EPS of $8.80, the $165.01 close implies 18.8x P/E; at 20.5x P/E, the close implies $8.05 EPS.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $8.80 (5.3 pp).
valuation.watch_metric: Commercial aftermarket vs. OE revenue mix and Engines & Power Systems operating margin as supply-chain constraints ease.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 2026 earnings release and FY2027 initial guidance (expected late January / early February 2027)

analyst_notes: Following HONA's June 29, 2026 spin-off and October 28, 2026 Q3 earnings release, Street sentiment shifted cautious: BMO downgraded to Market Perform (PT cut from $209 to $181) on October 29, and both Goldman Sachs ($190 to $180) and Jefferies ($175 to $170) trimmed targets on November 2, citing supply-chain constraints and margin headwinds. Morgan Stanley remains constructive (Overweight, $205 PT from August 19), viewing post-spin valuation as discounted. The three post-earnings Hold-rated targets ($170-$181) cluster tightly around our $180.40 base case (+9.3% vs. $165.01 close).
